Gaza remains gripped by daily violence, with the Israeli military and Hamas accusing each other of violating the truce in effect since 10 October. The war flattened swathes of the territory, displaced most of the population at least once, and left hundreds of thousands of people living in tents and temporary shelters. — Photograph: Eyad Baba/AFP/Getty Images

item.description:
Derbyshire, UK — Burnt ground at Tintwistle Moor in Glossop. One of England’s largest wildfires in recent years began on 24 June and burned an estimated 606 hectares (1,497 acres) of moorland and woodland. The fire, which was declared a major incident on 13 July, burned for more than six weeks before being brought under control. With 71% of England in drought, high-risk areas such as moorland across the Peak District are in urgent need of rain to prevent further wildfires. — Photograph: Brook Mitchell/Getty Images

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

The main military hospital is supported by the David Nott Foundation, a UK charity that has trained more than 1,000 Ukrainian surgeons, anaesthetists and other healthcare workers. The leaders of Luxembourg, Moldova and Estonia as well as António Costa, the European Council president, are also in Kyiv for the talks on Ukraine’s Independence Day, amid Russia’s latest escalation. — Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images

Arday’s family said in a statement: ‘Jason was subjected to a campaign of sustained abuse for more than three years since he accepted the role of professor at Cambridge University by those who would leave no stone unturned in their quest to undermine him. The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and always wanted to see the best in everyone’. — Photograph: Alishia Abodunde/Getty Images

Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks since the start of the war, causing a fire at a distribution warehouse near Moscow and killing at least six people overnight, according to Russian authorities. — Photograph: Tatyana Makeyeva/AFP/Getty Images

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

item.description:
Moscow, Russia — Drivers line up at a Lukoil petrol station in the capital, where many other stations have run out of fuel. Moscow confirmed this week that Russia was having to import refined petroleum products to try to stabilise supply following Ukraine’s attacks on its refineries. The Reuters news agency used industry contacts and market data to establish that a tanker from India had recently arrived and unloaded, while supplies were also being sourced from east Asia. — Photograph: Getty Images

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

item.title: [The Guardian — Photos of the Day] The week around the world in 20 pictures
item.source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day
item.description:
Kyiv, Ukraine — People take shelter and sleep inside a subway station during an air raid alert. Russia and Ukraine have been escalating long-range attacks recently while air defences remain short. Ukraine has attacked oil refineries and warehouses close to Moscow using newly developed cruise missiles and drones, while Russia has stepped up its attacks on Kyiv, making heavy use of hard ballistics. — Photograph: Kostiantyn Liberov/Libkos/Getty Images

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

The Ukrainian Book Institute has called on the international publishing community to support Ukrainian publishers after Russian attacks in July and early August destroyed about 10m books and a significant share of the country’s book production capacity. — Photograph: Efrem Lukatsky/AP
